questions.q: What is the difference between a class and an object?
options: A class is a blueprint; an object is one instance built from that blueprint
They're interchangeable terms for the same thing
A class can only hold numbers, an object can hold any type
An object is defined first, and a class is built from several objects
questions.explain: A class describes what a kind of thing looks like and does; each object (instance) is one real thing created from that blueprint, with its own data.

options: Only when you call it explicitly, like any other method
Automatically, every time a new instance of the class is created
Only once per program, no matter how many instances are created
Only when the object is deleted
questions.explain: Python automatically calls `__init__` right after building a new instance, which is where you typically set up that instance's starting attributes.

questions.q: What does `self` refer to inside an instance method?
options: The class itself, shared by every instance
A built-in Python module
The specific instance the method is being called on
The parent class in an inheritance chain
questions.explain: self is simply the first parameter of an instance method, automatically bound to whichever instance called it — it's how a method reads and writes that instance's own attributes.

questions.q: Given `msg1 = ChatMessage("user", "hi")` and `msg2 = ChatMessage("assistant", "hello")`, what happens to `msg1.content` when you later change `msg2.content`?
options: It also changes, since both were built from the same class
It raises an error
It stays unchanged, because each instance holds its own independent attributes
Both become `None`
questions.explain: Instance attributes (set via `self.x = ...` in `__init__`) are stored per-object. Two instances of the same class never share that data unless you deliberately point them at the same object.

questions.q: What is a class attribute, as opposed to an instance attribute?
options: A value defined directly under the class body (outside `__init__`) that's shared by every instance unless overridden
A value that can only ever be an integer
An attribute that gets deleted automatically after one use
An attribute that only exists on the very first instance created
questions.explain: Class attributes live on the class itself and are shared defaults across all instances, while instance attributes (set with `self.x = ...`) vary independently per object.
